findings.title: Secret-key depth is the first hit in sorted key order, not the shallowest
findings.detail: secretDepth walks the parsed canonical payload depth-first in sorted key order and returns the first hit. For {a:{password:1}, password:1} it reports depth 2, although a depth-1 secret key exists. The spec does not pin down which depth to report when there are several hits.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a payload holds secret-like keys at several depths, such as { a: { password: 1 }, password: 1 } THEN validateEvent throws AUDIT_PAYLOAD_SECRET with details.depth of the first hit in a depth-first walk in sorted key order (2 here).

findings.title: Size check runs before the secret-key scan
findings.detail: A payload over 32,768 canonical bytes that also holds a secret-named key is refused with AUDIT_EVENT_INVALID payload_too_large, not AUDIT_PAYLOAD_SECRET. No scenario fixes this precedence.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a payload whose canonical text exceeds 32,768 bytes also holds a secret-named key THEN validateEvent throws AUDIT_EVENT_INVALID with details.reason payload_too_large.

findings.title: An unknown property takes precedence over a bad eventType

findings.title: task 5.2: a head below the walked tip is reported as a hash failure instead of passing
findings.detail: Task 5.2 says a head whose seq is below the walked tip (tipSeq = expected - 1n) passes. In verify.ts, when headSeq < expected the code goes on to `if (lastHash === null || !lastHash.equals(head.hash)) return { ..., firstBadSeq: headSeq, reason: "hash" }`. lastHash is the tip's hash, not the head's, so a head below the tip always fails. The head is read in a separate statement before the walk. Unless withTenantTx uses a snapshot isolation level, an append committed between the head read and the walk makes an intact chain report a `hash` failure. That contradicts design.md: 'appends during a verification are not tail loss'.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare head.hash only when headSeq === expected - 1n, and let headSeq < expected - 1n pass.

findings.title: task 5.1: a stored row that canonicalEvent cannot hash makes verifyChain throw instead of reporting hash
findings.detail: Task 5.1 says chainHash not matching the stored hash, or canonicalEvent throwing, gives `hash`. verify.ts calls chainHash without a try/catch. An owner edit that canonicalEvent cannot hash makes verifyChain reject with an AuditError instead of returning {ok:false, reason:'hash'}. Two examples: `at` in year 10000, where to_char gives a five-digit year and the six-digit-fraction regex fails; and a payload number beyond the double range, where node-pg parses it as Infinity.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the chainHash call in try/catch and return { ok: false, checked, firstBadSeq: seq, reason: "hash" } when it throws.

findings.title: Unspecified: head seq below the visible tip
findings.detail: No scenario covers a head whose seq is below the last event the walk sees. That can happen through an owner rewind of the head or a concurrent append. Reasonable implementations differ: pass, or report hash at the head seq.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN the head's seq is below the seq of the last event the walk reads THEN verifyChain returns { ok: false, checked: <events walked>, firstBadSeq: <head seq>, reason: "hash" }.

findings.title: Unspecified: stored event whose fields canonicalEvent refuses
findings.detail: No scenario covers a stored row whose `at` year is above 9999 or whose jsonb number is outside the double range. The committed code throws instead of returning a report.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a stored audit_event row has an at in a year above 9999 THEN verifyChain rejects with AuditError AUDIT_EVENT_INVALID (details.reason bad_at) instead of returning a report.

findings.title: Secret-key depth is the first hit in sorted key order, not the shallowest
findings.detail: secretDepth walks the parsed canonical payload depth-first in sorted key order and returns the first hit. For {a:{password:1}, password:1} it reports depth 2, although a depth-1 secret key exists. The spec does not pin down which depth to report when there are several hits.
evidence: src/audit/event.ts secretDepth: for (const [key, item] of Object.entries(value)) { if (isSecretKeyName(key)) return depth; const found = secretDepth(item, depth + 1); ...
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a payload holds secret-like keys at several depths, such as { a: { password: 1 }, password: 1 } THEN validateEvent throws AUDIT_PAYLOAD_SECRET with details.depth of the first hit in a depth-first walk in sorted key order (2 here).

findings.title: Size check runs before the secret-key scan
findings.detail: A payload over 32,768 canonical bytes that also holds a secret-named key is refused with AUDIT_EVENT_INVALID payload_too_large, not AUDIT_PAYLOAD_SECRET. No scenario fixes this precedence.

findings.title: task 5.2: a head below the walked tip is reported as a hash failure instead of passing
findings.detail: Task 5.2 says a head whose seq is below the walked tip (tipSeq = expected - 1n) passes. In verify.ts, when headSeq < expected the code goes on to `if (lastHash === null || !lastHash.equals(head.hash)) return { ..., firstBadSeq: headSeq, reason: "hash" }`. lastHash is the tip's hash, not the head's, so a head below the tip always fails. The head is read in a separate statement before the walk. Unless withTenantTx uses a snapshot isolation level, an append committed between the head read and the walk makes an intact chain report a `hash` failure. That contradicts design.md: 'appends during a verification are not tail loss'.

findings.detail: Task 5.1 says chainHash not matching the stored hash, or canonicalEvent throwing, gives `hash`. verify.ts calls chainHash without a try/catch.
